title: The results we stand behind
question: Two accuracy results scored against real energy use the model did not see, and one agreement check against an independent solar model. The full studies follow below.

headline.label: Median error with a year of utility bills
headline.note: Calibrated on 2016 bills and scored on 2017, a year the model never saw. The same buildings were 18.1% off without bills.

headline.label: Median error on Los Angeles offices, from our own scans
headline.note: Annual energy use per square foot against the City of Los Angeles building benchmarking data, with no bills. A typical-office benchmark scores 16.5% on the same buildings.

headline.label: Solar output within 10% of an independent model
headline.note: Our predicted annual output per kilowatt for 76 scanned Los Angeles roofs, against PVGIS, the European Commission's solar model. The median difference is +2%. This shows two models agree; it is not a measured output.

caveats: The solar comparison is model against model, not a measured meter, and almost every roof was flat, so panel direction was barely tested.
Calibration to bills succeeds for 44 of 283 buildings today; the 4.1% applies to those 44.

Without bills, tuning the model's assumptions cannot make totals precise: even a correction fitted to the answers left most buildings more than 25% off. A year of the building's own bills is what makes it precise.
On offices we are only slightly better than a typical-office benchmark. Without bills, the model's value is which upgrades fit a building, not its total energy.
Savings from individual upgrades have not yet been checked against measured results.

provenance.sources: Building Data Genome Project 2 (bills result); City of Los Angeles EBEWE benchmarking and PVGIS (offices and solar), run on 15 November 2026
